cards.body:
*Lesson 1.1 · Your First Zap*

_≈ 90 minutes · with Miracle_

Welcome to Spark Street. Everything so far was thinking and planning; today you build an automation that runs by itself, 24 hours a day, while you do something else. It takes about 20 minutes once you know the moves.

*Your problem:* You do the same small task by hand every day.
*The plan:* Build your first Zap end to end: trigger, action, test, publish.
*After this lesson:* You'll have a working automation running on its own, in under an hour.

*Where's the tomato invoice?*

*Tuesday:* Month-end. The accountant wants all of October's supplier invoices.

*Two hours later:* Tolu has found 19 of 25. Three are in WhatsApp. One was deleted.

*Glitch:* "Invoices hide beautifully in a busy inbox."

*Bolt:* "Every invoice that ever lands should file itself. Let's build your first Zap."

*A Zap is a trigger plus actions*

Zapier's name for a workflow is a *Zap*. It's the trigger → action → outcome shape from Module 0.1, built from cards in the Zap editor. Each card needs four choices: the *app*, the *event*, the *account* to connect, and the *fields* to fill in.

*Instant or polling: when does your Zap wake up?*

Remember polling and webhooks from 0.2. Zapier labels triggers that use webhooks as *Instant*: they run within seconds. Other triggers, including Gmail's, *poll*: Zapier checks for new items on a timer. On the free plan that timer is 15 minutes; paid plans check more often.

*What that means for Tolu:* an invoice arriving at 10:02 might be filed at 10:15. For invoices that's fine. For a customer waiting on an order confirmation, you'd want an instant trigger (Modules 1.4 and 2.5).

*Field mapping: fixed text plus data pills*

When you fill in an action's fields, you can type fixed text, insert data from earlier steps, or mix both. Inserted data appears as a small labelled chip, often called a *pill*. At run time, each pill is replaced with that run's real value.

_A file name built from pills and fixed text:_
- *Pill · From Name*: Farmgate Supplies
- *Text*: -
- *Pill · Subject*: Invoice 0192
- *Text*: -
- *Pill · Attachment Name*: inv_0192.pdf

*Nodo:* Every pill is a path into the trigger's JSON from Module 0.3. Zapier just gives the paths friendly names. Watch the type too: a _file_ pill carries the actual file, while a name or link pill is only text.

*Tasks: what Zapier counts and charges*

A *task* is one action that runs successfully. Checking for new data doesn't count, failed actions don't count, and Zapier's built-in tools (such as Filter, Formatter, Paths and Delay) don't use tasks either.

_Free plan, as of Oct 2026 · What it means here_
- *100 tasks a month* · 25 invoices a month = 25 tasks. Plenty of room.
- *Two-step Zaps (one trigger, one action)* · Today's Zap fits exactly. Multi-step Zaps need a paid plan or a trial.
- *15 minutes between checks* · Invoices file within a quarter of an hour.

Plans change. Check zapier.com/pricing before you advise a client; new accounts often start with a trial of paid features.

*Draft, publish, and Zap history*

- *Test*: Runs one step once with sample data, so you can check the result before going live.
- *Publish*: Turns the Zap on. Until then, nothing runs by itself, however perfect your tests.
- *Edits*: Changes to a published Zap stay in draft until you publish again.
- *Zap history*: A log of every run, showing its status plus the exact data in and out of each step. Your first stop when something looks wrong.

cards.body:
*Solved problem: supplier invoices file themselves*

*The goal.* Every attachment in an email labelled *Invoices* is saved to a Google Drive folder called *Supplier invoices*, with a file name that says who it's from and what it is. Build it in the business Google account from Module 0.6, not your personal one.

*Step 1 · Prepare Gmail: a label that fills itself*

In Gmail, create a label called *Invoices*. Then create a filter (Settings → Filters and blocked addresses → Create a new filter) that matches your suppliers' addresses and "has attachment", and applies the Invoices label. Now Gmail does the sorting and Zapier only has to watch one label.

*Sage:* *Fix the input first* (Module 0.1). A tidy label is easier and cheaper than asking an automation, or an AI, to guess which emails are invoices.

*Step 2 · Create the Zap and set the trigger*

In Zapier, create a new Zap. For the trigger choose app *Gmail* and event *New Attachment*. Connect the business Gmail account, and read the permission screen before allowing (0.6). In the trigger's options:

_Field · Set to · Why_
- *Label/Mailbox* · Invoices · Only watch the label your filter fills.
- *Search String* · `-in:sent` · Ignore attachments you sent yourself.

*Step 3 · Test the trigger with a real email*

Email yourself a small PDF from another address, and make sure it lands in the Invoices label. Click *Test trigger*. Zapier finds the email and shows its fields: From Name, Subject, Date, the attachment file, and more. Pick that record to use as sample data for the next step.

*Step 4 · Add the action and map the fields*

Add an action: app *Google Drive*, event *Upload File*. Connect the same business account. Then:

_Field · Set to_
- *Drive* · My Google Drive
- *Folder* · Harvest Lane → Supplier invoices (create it first)
- *File* · The *attachment file* pill from step 1 (not the attachment's name or link)
- *File name* · From Name pill + " - " + Subject pill + " - " + Attachment name pill

Zapier sometimes renames fields. If a label doesn't match, choose the closest option; for the File field, pick the entry marked as a file.

*Step 5 · Test, name, publish*

Click *Test step*, then open Drive: the PDF should be in Supplier invoices with the new name. Rename the Zap to *HL · Invoices → Drive* (a naming habit that pays off at 30 Zaps) and click *Publish*.

*Step 6 · Prove it works live, then read the history*

Send another test invoice. Within about 15 minutes on the free plan it appears in Drive with no clicks from you. Open *Zap history*, click the run, and look at the data that went into and out of each step. This is how you'll debug everything from now on.

- *2* steps, fits the free plan
- *≈25* tasks a month for Tolu's volume
- *0 min* of Tolu's time per invoice from now on

*Why this approach works*

- Gmail's filter does the sorting, so the Zap stays simple.
- A consistent file name makes month-end a search, not a hunt.
- Testing with a real email gives real sample data to map.
- Zap history lets you verify every future run.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Mapping the attachment _name_ into the File field (you get a text file).
- Forgetting to publish after a successful test.
- Connecting a personal account "just to try".
- Watching the whole inbox instead of one label.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* I built the same Zap for a friend's shop. Here are four complaints from the owner. Match each to its cause.

*A:* Drive fills with tiny text files that contain a web link, not the PDFs.
*B:* Quotes the owner _sent_ to customers are being saved as supplier invoices.
*C:* Every file is called "attachment", so they overwrite each other's meaning.
*D:* The test worked perfectly on Monday; by Thursday not one new invoice has been saved, and Zap history is empty.

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
*A:* the File field was mapped to a text pill (the attachment's name or link) instead of the file itself.
*B:* the Search String `-in:sent` was removed, and the Zap watches all mail instead of the Invoices label.
*C:* the file name is fixed text. Build it from pills: sender, subject, attachment name.
*D:* the Zap was tested but never published (or was turned off). No runs means Zap history stays empty.

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): Form orders land in the sheet
cards.body:
- Make a short Google Form: name, phone, product, quantity, delivery date.
- Build a Zap: *Google Forms · New Form Response* → *Google Sheets · Create Spreadsheet Row* into the Orders table from 0.4 (a copy is fine).
- Map each form answer to the right column. Submit three test orders.

*Done when:*
- Three rows appear with every value in the right column, and Zap history shows three successful runs.

cards.answer:
- *Columns don't appear in the Zap:* the sheet needs its header row in row 1 (rule 1 from 0.4). Refresh the fields after fixing it.
- *Phone loses its zero:* format the phone column as plain text in Sheets (0.4).

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): A new order alerts Tolu
cards.body:
- Build a second Zap: *Google Sheets · New Spreadsheet Row* in Orders → *Gmail · Send Email* to yourself.
- Make the subject combine three pills with text, e.g. `New order · Mrs Adebayo · 2026-10-06`.
- In the body, list every field of the order on its own line.

*Done when:*
- Submitting the Bronze form sends you the email automatically. You've just chained two Zaps: the form fills the sheet, and the sheet sends the alert.

cards.answer: Two two-step Zaps connected through a sheet let you do multi-step work on the free plan, at the cost of a delay (the sheet trigger polls) and two tasks per order. In 1.2 you'll build it as one multi-step Zap instead.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): Your own first automation
cards.body:
- Pick the top-scoring task from your Module 0.1 Silver mission, or another task that fits a two-step Zap.
- Draw its map, build it, test it with three real items, publish it, and let it run for a week.
- After a week, check Zap history: count runs, failures and tasks used, and estimate time saved.

*Done when:*
- It has run live at least five times, and you've written up runs, tasks and minutes saved in your log.

cards.q: On the free plan, how quickly will a polling Gmail trigger notice a new email?
cards.why: Polling triggers check on a timer; the free plan checks every 15 minutes.

cards.q: Which of these uses a task?
options: Zapier checking Gmail for new mail
Successfully uploading a file to Drive
cards.why: A task is a successful action. Polling, failures and built-in tools like Filter don't count.

cards.q: Drive fills with small text files containing a link. What went wrong?
options: A text pill was mapped into the File field
cards.why: The File field needs the file pill. A name or link pill is just text, so Zapier saves it as a text file.

cards.q: Your Zap tested perfectly yesterday, but nothing has run since. What's the first thing to check?
options: Whether the Zap is published and on
cards.why: Testing doesn't turn a Zap on. Publishing does.

cards.q: Where do you see the exact data that went in and out of each step on a past run?
cards.why: Zap history logs every run with its status and data. It's your debugger.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. Every Zap card needs an app, an event, an account and fields.
2. Instant triggers use webhooks; polling ones check on a timer (15 minutes on free).
3. Fields mix fixed text with pills; check the pill's type (file vs. text).
4. A task is one successful action; built-in tools and failures don't count.
5. Test, then publish. Nothing runs until you publish.
6. Zap history is your debugger.

*Lesson 1.1 complete!* _Your First Zap_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Lesson 1.2, _Multi-Step Zaps & Formatter_.
